scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): grants the weight of expert judgment, then argues non-experts offer valuable criticism too; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: When a film or a book is reviewed, we often ask whether the critic really knows the subject.
Some people argue that critical judgment of work in any field has little value unless it comes from an expert in that field.
I agree that expert judgment carries special weight, but I believe non-experts can also offer valuable criticism.

sections.role: Body 1 — Why expert judgment carries weight

sentences.text: First, judgment from a true expert often does carry the greatest weight.
An expert understands the deep rules and history of a field that outsiders may miss entirely.
For example, a trained musician can hear subtle mistakes in a performance that most listeners never notice.
This shows that expert knowledge can reveal qualities and flaws hidden from ordinary view.
Experts can also compare a new work fairly against the best that has come before.
Their judgment is harder to fool with mere tricks or surface appeal.
To this extent, expert criticism is genuinely valuable.
Second, however, valuable judgment can also come from people who are not experts.
Ordinary audiences, after all, are the very people most art and work is created to serve.
Consider how the lasting popularity of a film with everyday viewers can reveal a worth critics missed.
Such reactions show that non-experts often sense honestly what truly moves or helps people.
Fresh eyes can also notice problems that experts, lost in detail, have stopped seeing.
A customer's plain opinion of a product can be as useful as any expert's report.
Useful judgment, then, is not limited to experts alone.
In conclusion, expert criticism deserves special respect for its depth and knowledge.
But the honest reactions of ordinary people also carry real and useful value.
The wisest view weighs both expert judgment and the voice of those a work is meant to serve.
